item.title: Made By AI :: [AI] [WIP] A new kind of porting - Chrono Runner (from MSX)
item.description:
Author: tachyMC
Subject: [AI] [WIP] A new kind of porting - Chrono Runner (from MSX)
Posted: Sat Nov 14, 2026 3:27 pm (GMT 0)

How I got the idea

Hi all folks,

I am a long time SMS fan, but never got proficient enough in C programming to create games for the platform.

With the advent of LLM-augmented programming, I finally got a tool which I could use to bring my favourite games to the SMS, but... I realized that I still needed graphics and sounds :)

Let me introduce Chrono Runner, a game developed by the Italian MSX developer association, for the MSX1 platform. It competed in the MSXDev25 game development contest (I cannot post links yet, look for "msxdev" and "Chrono Runner" on Google).

You play a time-travelling runner who can rewind time to undo mistakes and try a different path.

To my glad surprise, the authors decided to make the game 100% open source, code and assets (I cannot post links yet, look for "Chrono-runners" on GitHub).

The current state

For the past few weeks I’ve been working on a Master System port, and I’d like to share some work-in-progress screenshots.

Playable in emulators from the title screen to the final boss, with music and sound effects. Still missing: an instructions screen redrawn for the pad, the intro logo, and testing on real hardware. Still present: some bugs that I'm trying to iron out!

A new kind of porting

Why do I mention this is a new kind of porting? Because I tried the recompile instead of the rewrite approach. Let me explain.

Instead of asking the LLM to rewrite the game from scratch, I asked it to keep the the original C code (written with MSXgl). The code is recompiled, almost unchanged with SDCC and devkitSMS, on top of a compatibility layer that implements the part of the MSXgl API the game uses.

Admittedly, four of the original source files needed some nontrivial changes. In short:

Graphics: the Graphic 2 tileset is converted 1:1 to Mode 4 tiles at build time, so the original screen layouts and level data are used as they are.

Sprites: the 32 single-colour 16x16 planes of the TMS9918 are emulated. Each plane becomes two 8x16 SMS sprites, so the SMS limit of 8 per line matches the MSX limit of 4 per line exactly. Coloured tiles are generated on the fly from the original 1-bit patterns and cached in VRAM.

Game logic: MSXgl’s pawn and state machine modules are ported, the pad is read as an MSX joystick, and the ASCII16 ROM segments map onto SMS banks.

Audio: the original PT3 tunes and ayFX sound effects are played by the same MSXgl players. Every frame, the AY-3-8910 register image is translated for the SN76489.
[/list]


The nice side effect is that the compatibility layer isn’t specific to Chrono Runner!!! It could make porting other MSXgl-based MSX games to the Master System much easier.

By the way, thanks to sverx for devkitSMS and to aoineko for MSXgl, which made this possible.

Feedback is very welcome on the approach. If you like the idea, I will gladly spend the extra time (and tokens!) required to refine both the revised Chrono Runner source, and the msxgl / sms layer source, and release the ROM along with the full source.
